prompt.context: Your client, East Oak, is a fast-growing retailer of modern home goods and furnishings. The company has seen tremendous growth over the past 5 years and is considering ways to continue this growth. The CEO is looking for our team to provide recommendations for how to achieve this.
prompt.question: How should East Oak achieve a 10% increase in revenue (approximately $24M)?

clarifying_info.q: What distribution channels does East Oak currently use?
How does East Oak handle fulfillment?
clarifying_info.a: 100% dropship — does not own any inventory; purchases items from manufacturers and ships directly to the customer.
Some big box stores like Target and Amazon, but mostly higher-end retailers like West Elm and Crate and Barrel.

clarifying_info.q: What is East Oak's current annual revenue?
Where does East Oak currently ship?
clarifying_info.a: Currently only ships in the U.S.
No specific timeline; as soon as possible.

exhibits.title: Consumer Ratings
exhibits.shows: A table comparing East Oak, Competitor 1, and the Industry Average across six dimensions rated on a 1-5 scale (1=bad, 5=good).

exhibits.title: Investment Options For East Oak
exhibits.shows: A chart listing five investment options with their associated project costs and NPV values; all figures in millions.

framework: Revenue = Price x Volume; explore levers under each
Price: product margins, price increases, shipping fees, product range (low to high)
Volume: product mix and quality of assortment, variety and product types, number of suppliers, number of styles, top-selling products, product availability and stock
Other: improve user/customer experience (web design, faster shipping, better customer service, return policy, VR/AI), brand partnerships and marketing
Note: costs should not be included in the framework since the prompt specifically asks about revenue growth

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. Which dimensions should East Oak focus on and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should immediately identify the three below-benchmark dimensions: Product Selection (2.7 vs 4.3 competitor, 3.9 industry average), Price (3.3 vs 3.4 competitor, 3.8 industry average), and Availability (4.1 vs 4.7 competitor, 4.3 industry average). Candidate should also note East Oak's strengths in Product Quality (4.8) and Customer Service (4.2). A strong candidate recognizes that a low Price score signals customers perceive items as too expensive, and that low Selection and Availability scores may be linked and could be addressed together.

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 2. Which investments should East Oak prioritize to reach its $24M revenue goal?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute a profitability ratio (NPV / Project Cost) for each option, rank them, and select investments that cumulatively reach $24M NPV. A strong candidate immediately discards options with ratio below 1.0 (Acquire Furniture Manufacturer and Acquire Competitor) since they destroy value. An excellent candidate identifies that combining Technology for Inventory Management and Private Label Products yields $25M NPV total, just clearing the $24M goal at a combined cost of only $7M, and flags funding considerations (cash vs. debt).

math.setup: Profitability ratio = NPV / Project Cost for each option
steps: Rank by ratio: Tech (3.67) > Private Label (3.50) > Build Facility (1.25) > Acquire Manufacturer (0.90) > Acquire Competitor (0.76)
Select top two: Tech NPV $11M + Private Label NPV $14M = $25M, exceeds $24M goal
math.answer: Invest in Technology for Inventory Management and Private Label Products; combined NPV = $25M, exceeding the $24M goal by $1M at a total cost of $7M.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways in which East Oak can improve on product selection and availability?

categories.name: Existing Supply Chain
ideas: Work with existing suppliers to procure more product and reduce out-of-stocks
Use technology to improve inventory management

categories.name: Private Label Risks (follow-up)
ideas: Manufacturing: difficulty getting exclusivity rights; risk competitors will copy products
Financial: lower prices may compress margins; could cannibalize higher-margin products; increased marketing spend required
Operational: product quality may be lower than existing assortment; limited in-house design capabilities and expertise

recommendation: East Oak should invest in a technology solution for inventory management ($3M cost, $11M NPV) and launch private label products ($4M cost, $14M NPV)
These two investments together deliver $25M in NPV, slightly exceeding the $24M revenue growth goal (10% of $240M)
risks: Actual returns may be lower than NPV estimates, potentially falling short of the $24M goal
Sufficient cash or access to capital must be secured to fund the $7M investment
Competitor response (e.g., copying the private label, aggressive pricing)
Private label could cannibalize margins on existing higher-priced products
next_steps: Identify suppliers and manufacturers for the private label program
Evaluate and select technology platforms for inventory management
Conduct sensitivity analysis on NPV and cost projections
Assess financing options (cash on hand vs. debt) for the $7M outlay
